key_points: NVIDIA researchers propose five guidelines for optimizing speculative decoding in AI model co-design.
The authors report that speculative decoding accelerates inference by predicting multiple tokens per iteration using a draft model.
Guideline one suggests increasing draft length to push GEMMs into a compute-bound region without increasing KV cache capacity pressure.
Guideline two recommends choosing a draft length equal to 128 divided by the number of query heads per KV head minus one when attention dominates.
The authors advise benchmarking acceptance length and draft overhead under realistic serving conditions to select the optimal draft mechanism.
items.summary: NVIDIA researchers present a guide for accelerating large language model inference through speculative decoding while maintaining accuracy. The authors report that this technique predicts multiple tokens per iteration using a small draft model to verify outputs in parallel with a larger target model. They provide five specific guidelines for selecting draft length and mechanism across the Pareto frontier. First, increase draft length to push GEMMs into a compute-bound region without increasing KV cache pressure. Second, when attention dominates decode time, choose a draft length calculated as 128 divided by the number of query heads per KV head minus one. Third, prefer draft lengths where the product of query heads and draft length plus one is a multiple of 128 to avoid tile underutilization. Fourth, at very low latency, increase draft length only while the gain in acceptance length justifies the added draft cost. Finally, choose the draft mechanism by balancing acceptance length and draft overhead for the specific workload and hardware. The authors recommend using SPEED-Bench for acceptance measurements and NVIDIA TensorRT LLM for quantifying draft overhead.
items.title: NVIDIA outlines five guidelines for co-designing AI models using speculative decoding

items.summary: U.S. uranium production reached 2.13 million pounds in the first half of 2026, yet domestic output remains a small fraction of reactor fuel needs. items.summary: The article explores how Uttam Kumar remains a defining figure in Bengali cinema decades after his death. Critics found the 2024 film Oti Uttam apathetic, yet it became a box-office hit that proved his magic still enchants audiences. Uttam Kumar died in 1980 at age 53, but his name remains synonymous with Bengali cinema and culture. His career began with eight flops between 1948 and 1952 before he achieved stardom with Basu Paribar in 1952. He formed an iconic pairing with Suchitra Sen, appearing together in 30 films over 22 years. Unlike many stars, Uttam played darker, flawed characters and took supporting roles for artistic reasons. Satyajit Ray cast him in Nayak, portraying a middle-class youth, and later in Chiriyakhana as Byomkesh Bakshi. Soumitra Chatterjee acknowledged Uttam's unmatched popularity, comparing their rivalry to rival football clubs. Uttam represented the honest, middle-class Bengali man and became a symbol of Bengaliness. His mass adulation is compared to that of Rudolph Valentino in Hollywood. As Satyajit Ray noted, there will never be another like Uttam Kumar.
items.title: Uttam Kumar's enduring legacy shines in Bengali cinema and culture

items.summary: An author reproduces a viral watercolour painting project originally created by Surya Narreddi, implementing the full training pipeline using TRL and OpenEnv. items.summary: WIRED analyzed Flock Safety's AI-powered surveillance software, which allows police to search video feeds using written descriptions of people. The company recently implemented new safeguards after facing backlash over misuse, including a Texas deputy searching 83,000 cameras for a woman who had an abortion. However, experts warn that Flock's guardrails may discourage but not stop abusive uses. The AI model, running on Flock's servers, decides which descriptions officers can search for without departmental oversight. While the system blocks searches based on race and religion, it only warns against political and cultural expression, a category experts say is heavily protected under the First Amendment. Flock states that officers cannot run prohibited searches, but the company did not explain how warnings are triggered for religion and nationality. Data flows both ways, with Flock receiving officer search queries and subsequent actions, though the company did not disclose how long these records are kept. Over 46 of 50 recent officer misconduct cases involving license plate readers involved Flock. Flock claims local agencies set rules, but critics argue the technology enables mass surveillance that requires structural reform beyond targeting individual bad actors.

items.summary: Researchers published a study in Communications Earth & Environment arguing that limiting global warming to well below 2°C requires stringent methane reductions alongside net-zero CO2 targets. items.summary: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune announced the reinstatement of the death penalty for arsonists following unprecedented wildfires that devastated forests and killed dozens. Tebboune attributed the fires to climate change but also ordered investigations into criminal responsibility. The government declared the region a disaster area and mobilized resources for relief and reconstruction.
items.title: Algerian President Tebboune seeks death penalty for arsonists amid deadly wildfires

items.title: Everton transfer fails as Balogun withdraws over health doubts

key_points: Czech President Petr Pavel stated Russia uses sabotage and disinformation to weaken trust in European institutions.
Pavel explained Moscow avoids direct military attacks on NATO in favor of hybrid tactics like airspace violations and provocations.
Czech officials are updating notification systems for Russian diplomats after Germany reported an explosive drone incident.
Prime Minister Andrej Babis affirmed Czechia's readiness to cooperate with European and transatlantic partners on security.
items.summary: Czech President Petr Pavel told CNN that Russia employs sabotage and disinformation to undermine European trust and divide member states. He noted Moscow resorts to these hybrid tactics because it cannot launch an open attack on NATO. Pavel argued that this strategy has backfired by strengthening EU and NATO unity. Meanwhile, Czech authorities are tightening monitoring of Russian diplomats following German accusations regarding a drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport. Foreign Minister Petr Macinka and Prime Minister Andrej Babis confirmed preparations for new security measures and pledged cooperation with partners.
items.title: Czech President Says Russia Uses Hybrid Tactics to Divide Europe

key_points: Pemex and Petrobras announced a two-year partnership to explore oilfields in the Gulf of Mexico.
Environmental groups fear the deal commits both nations to fossil fuel production and increases spill risks.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum emphasized renewable energy investment over the oil deal.
items.summary: Pemex and Petrobras announced a two-year partnership to explore mature and deepwater oilfields in the Gulf of Mexico. Environmental campaigners warn the agreement risks decades of fossil fuel emissions and pollution near vulnerable reef habitats. The deal follows recent safety incidents at Mexican petrochemical sites, with some hoping Petrobras can share safety expertise. However, researchers note that deeper drilling increases spill risks and could displace coastal communities. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum downplayed the partnership, emphasizing renewable energy goals instead. Both companies declined to provide further details on the memorandum of understanding.
items.title: Mexico and Brazil state oil firms sign deal raising ecological concerns

key_points: Pierre Damas Bel died by suicide after being struck by a truck while wearing an ICE ankle monitor.
His family and advocates link his death to the psychological harm and social stigma caused by the device.
Amica filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration regarding the indiscriminate use of GPS monitors on approximately 50,000 people.
ICE stated it does not comment on causes of death during investigations and emphasized that undocumented immigrants have the option to self-deport.
items.summary: Pierre Damas Bel, a 20-year-old Haitian man, died by suicide after walking onto a highway where he was struck by a truck. His family attributes his death to the psychological distress caused by an electronic ankle monitor placed on him by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Lauren Hodges, a senior attorney at Amica, stated that such devices cause significant mental health deterioration and social stigma. The article notes that under the current administration, ICE now uses these monitors indiscriminately rather than evaluating cases individually. Bel's father reported that his son felt treated like an animal and faced harassment from peers due to the device. ICE did not comment on the cause of death while the investigation is ongoing but reiterated that undocumented immigrants can self-deport. The tragedy occurred after the termination of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians, leaving many without legal options to remain in the United States.
items.title: Pierre Damas Bel's death highlights psychological harm of ICE ankle monitors

items.title: Colombian woman leads grassroots effort to protect Andean condors

items.title: Nepal flood victims' families hold symbolic cremations after eight days

Jaishankar is on a three-day visit to Ukraine and Poland to conduct bilateral consultations with Ukrainian and Polish officials.
India has raised concerns over recent Russian strikes that killed an Indian citizen in Kyiv and attacks on merchant vessels in the Black Sea.

key_points: Meta agreed to lock out US teens under 18 from Instagram and Facebook between midnight and 6 am as part of a settlement.
The settlement also mandates a two-hour daily usage cap and hides like counts by default for teenagers.
Meta has not confirmed whether the US midnight lockout or other settlement terms will apply to India.
India already enforces a sleep mode for teens from 10 pm to 7 am, which is narrower than the US restriction.
Indian parents can manually configure screen-time limits and block access during chosen hours without default enforcement.
items.summary: Meta reached a settlement with US attorneys general requiring midnight-to-6 am lockouts for teens under 18. The deal includes daily usage caps and hidden like counts, effective for a decade. Meta has not announced plans to extend these specific US restrictions to India. India currently operates a narrower 10 pm to 7 am sleep mode for teen accounts. Parents in India can manually set screen-time limits and block access during specific hours.
items.title: Meta settles US teen lawsuits with midnight lockout; India rules differ

The agreement aims to expand market access and deepen economic ties between the two nations.
items.title: India delays US trade deal until preferential tariff terms are granted

key_points: India's 2016 drought manual uses multiple indicators, but inconsistent implementation and staffing gaps mean many drought-hit areas go undetected.
Past El Niño years cut agricultural output by 5 to 7%, and 315 districts are now flagged as vulnerable to current conditions.
Research indicates that drought relief is sometimes misdirected to benefit ruling state parties electorally rather than reaching the most vulnerable farmers.
The India Meteorological Department confirmed that El Niño is expected to gain strength over the second half of the monsoon season.
items.summary: India faces heightened drought risks as El Niño strengthens, yet systemic flaws in the declaration process leave many affected areas undetected. The 2016 drought manual relies on multiple indicators, but inconsistent implementation and staffing shortages hinder effective relief distribution. Past El Niño events reduced agricultural output by 5 to 7%, and current forecasts indicate a 14% rainfall deficit since the monsoon began. Political factors often influence drought declarations, with research showing relief may be misdirected for electoral gain. While the Indian Council on Agricultural Research advises on climate-resilient seeds, 315 districts remain vulnerable, and only 10 central financial assistance requests were made between 2020 and 2025.
items.title: El Niño threatens India's crops as drought declaration gaps persist

key_points: Cases of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and asthma have been rising in the last two decades.

The authors suggest that urban planning strategies prioritizing green spaces can help promote healthier immune system development.
items.summary: The authors report that cases of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases have risen over the last two decades. They argue that a disconnect from nature contributes to immune dysregulation, potentially leading to conditions like asthma and rheumatoid arthritis. The commentary suggests today's children face greater risks due to rapid urbanization and reduced outdoor exposure. Scientists propose that the immune system requires microbial diversity from natural environments to develop proper tolerance. The authors note that urban planning strategies prioritizing green spaces could support healthier immune system development in future generations.
items.title: Reduced nature exposure linked to rising immune system diseases in children

items.title: GJC urges balancing economic patriotism with cultural gold traditions

key_points: ANU Professor Alan Gamlen argues that migration is a defining force of the 21st century that transforms lives and enriches societies while also generating genuine pressures.
He states that the public debate wrongly frames migration as a binary choice between being for or against it, rather than focusing on how it can be managed well.

Gamlen notes that migration creates risks and rewards on both sides of the journey, expanding labour forces and introducing new ideas while potentially causing housing shortages if infrastructure is not prepared.
He emphasizes that most international migrants move through ordinary pathways for work or family reasons, not as refugees, and that forced displacement remains a severe global problem.
items.summary: ANU Professor Alan Gamlen argues that migration is a defining force of the 21st century that transforms lives and enriches societies while also generating genuine pressures. He states that the public debate wrongly frames migration as a binary choice between being for or against it, rather than focusing on how it can be managed well. Gamlen notes that migration creates risks and rewards on both sides of the journey, expanding labour forces and introducing new ideas while potentially causing housing shortages if infrastructure is not prepared. He emphasizes that most international migrants move through ordinary pathways for work or family reasons, not as refugees, and that forced displacement remains a severe global problem. The professor concludes that the sensible political question is not whether migration is good or bad, but whether governments are managing it competently through safe, orderly, and regular movement.
items.title: Migration is not a crisis or a cure-all. It just needs to be managed

items.summary: Welspun Corp shares rose 6% after Jefferies initiated coverage with a Buy rating, implying a 27% upside from its reference price.
